findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards logged output
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/fake.go returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver. LoggerMiddleware now does m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so when tests inject a TestLogger the Info/Warn/Error call goes to a fresh throwaway instance. The original TestLogger under test never records Calls/Message/Ctx, making log assertions impossible and hiding regressions.

findings.title: Missing nil-request guard causes panic before LoggerMiddleware
findings.body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics in contextual_logger_middleware.go dereference req.PluginContext and req fields unconditionally. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly checks if req == nil and bypasses logging, proving nil requests are expected. Because ContextualLoggerMiddleware is ordered outer to LoggerMiddleware, a nil request panics in instrumentContext path before reaching the nil-safe logger.

findings.title: MetricsMiddleware dereferences nil request
findings.body: MetricsMiddleware.QueryData in metrics_middleware.go does for _, v := range req.Queries and CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics access req.PluginContext/req.Body without a nil check. The sibling LoggerMiddleware handles req == nil, so nil is a valid input. Placed outer in the chain, this middleware will panic with nil dereference on such requests.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to Logger interface breaks implementers
findings.body: Logger interface in pkg/plugins/log/ifaces.go gains a new required method FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger. Any existing implementation of plugins/log.Logger outside this PR (other mocks, wrappers, external code) will fail to compile. Adding a method to a public interface is a breaking API change and requires updating all implementers or providing a default.

findings.title: Fragile type assertion silently drops contextual logger
findings.body: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext in pkg/plugins/log/logger.go does d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger) and on failure returns d.New() with no attributes. If the infra logger returns a different implementation of its Logger interface or nil, all contextual attributes added by ContextualLoggerMiddleware (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) are silently discarded and the Plugin Request Completed log loses its correlation fields.
